reviews.comment: I found this class relatively easy but its not a free A or B, you must put in the work. Decent amount of reading, not horrendous but still a lot. Attendance and participation in class was a minor part of your grade. If you don't go to lecture you could still pass but it would be difficult. Class had 3 exams, 9 assignments, and a paper/presentation

Professor Harmel is a really good professor if you put in the work and learn the material both in and out of class. I highly recommend using online note-taking resources like word because his lectures move fast and are usually long. There are luckily a few homework assignments that are pretty easy to do, though they require the book to access.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While Harmel can be a somewhat tough grader on writing, most of the work you do for him tends to be data analysis and concept memory. He gives clear directions on all of his assignments and the lectures are long but extremely helpful for the exams

Loved this class. Probably my favorite POLS class I took during my undergrad. Interesting and easy to follow lectures. Definitely not a blow off class though. 3 Cumulative exams with a term paper at the end and an easy homework assignment every 2-3 classes. Biggest thing is you've got to go to lecture. He takes attendance every class.

The class wasn't horrible but if you truly aren't interested in political parties I wouldn't recommend it. All test are cumulative and you have to do the reading or you are guaranteed a 70 or below on the test. There are an insane amount of readings that need to be completed.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I would take Harmel again. If you do the readings, show up to lectures, and participate now and then, you'll be fine. Harmel also does review sessions before each exam and most of the questions he goes over will show up. Sometimes the lectures could be a little dry, but he keeps you engaged by asking questions.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Exams are incredibly hard and you have to read about 20 articles per exam. Professor is really nice but the class is just hard in general

I wouldn't recommend taking him unless you are good at memorizing a bunch of articles, books, and lecture notes for the 3 exams. You need the textbook for homework, which are easy to do. Lectures are interesting and you are required to attend class. Term papers are easy and you have to do a presentation on your term paper at the end of the year.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Harmel's lectures he makes them interesting and is great at reviewing material. Do ALL of the readings and study a good week in advance (because there's a lot of material) and you'll be fine. Not particularly difficult, you just get what you put into it.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was sort of interesting, not what I expected tho. He answers emails so fast and seems really kind, but was all asynchronous. I would watch all the lectures like the day before & should have read more, got Bs on tests. Homework was easy, tests were short and hard. I pulled out the A bc of homework & the final paper! so work hard on that.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is graded really heavily on the exams which are 25 questions each in 30 minutes, he lets you use your notes but you don't have sufficient time to use them so its really pointless. He also grades pretty hard for giving little to no explanation on any of the assignments he gives. He responds to emails fast though.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Harmel is a really solid professor, smart and interesting. The class is pretty fun, and the lectures weren't boring. Not a hard class whatsoever, but definitely need to put the effort in. Make sure to stay on top of the schedule and you'll be fine. I'd definitely recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Harmel is one of my favorite professors in the political science department. His tests are difficult, cumulative and focus heavily on readings outside of class. He's very serious about political parties and certainly makes you work for an A, but if you manage to do well on the tests, you'll be fine.

Dr. Harmel is an incredible professor. His contributions to the study of political parties are well noted in the literature and his lectures are very thorough. He co-lectured one class with a professor from Norway, with whom he was collaborating on a book. There was a lot of reading and one large term paper, but it was so worth it.

Harmel is easily one of the most frustrating professors at A&M. Although there is a lot of material covered in the class it's not difficult to memorize. However, his tests are designed to trip you up. I'm a hard worker and knew all the reviews, studied for weeks in advance, and still got low C's on all the tests. Would not recommend to anyone.

As a POLS major, I very much enjoyed Dr. Harmel's course! However, you do have to study a lot to do well on tests, but as long as you go to class and do the readings, you should get an A or a B in the course. I would easily take him again.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.
